newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open mixed, seen seeking direction.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open mixed, seen seeking direction.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened little changed in very quiet trade on Tuesday with the market seen largely awaiting direction from upcoming economic news and data, analysts said.

"There was some overnight buying in our seven to 10 year term, but light buying. Activity in the long end is virtually negligible. There's just about nothing going on here in Canada," said Hank Cunningham, director of fixed-income for First Marathon Securities Ltd.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.13 to C$116.47 to yield 6.716 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 5/32 to yield 6.69 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to three basis points from nil at Monday's close.

"We're lacking news until the Fed meeting really. We've got (U.S.) consumer confidence coming up at 10 o'clock and that may give the market a little bit of direction, but the bottom line here is that the market is trying to find a comfort zone," said David Adamo, managing director of fixed income research with Scotia Capital Markets.
Activity was especially light with Quebec traders away for the St Jean Baptiste Day public and market holiday in Quebec.

In economic news, Statistics Canada reported that department stores sales rose a seasonally adjusted 1.2 percent in May from April, and the number of Canadians who applied for employment insurance benefits rose 0.4 percent in April from March. The numbers did not have a significant effect on the market.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.05 to C$108.26 to yield 6.126 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent which rose 3/32 to yield 6.41 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 28 basis points from 27 basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.82 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.14 percent.
